title: feat(types): name InputShorthandSchema and UiCalendarSchema on the ./zod barrel (objectui#9067)
body:
Fixes #9067

Implements the recorded ruling (director seat, decision batch #121 item 5, maintainer 2026-09-12): the **split**. Two of objectui#8499's four arms are named on the `./zod` barrel; two are recorded `ABSENT_BY_DECISION` with the reason, in the tree.

## The two newly exported symbols

`packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts` now exports, by name, for the first time:

| symbol | declared in | `type` literals it stands for |
|---|---|---|
| **`InputShorthandSchema`** | `zod/form.zod.ts` | `email`, `password` |
| **`UiCalendarSchema`** | `zod/form.zod.ts` | `ui:calendar` |

That is the entire movement on the published surface. Both schemas already existed, were already maintained and were already applied by `AnyComponentSchema`; only the barrel line is new, so a consumer can finally validate one of those node types **on its own** — the question `AnyComponentSchema` cannot answer, because it only answers "is this SOME valid node".

`Clause-②: yes`, declared by the ruling itself. `needs:contract-review` is hung on this PR.

## What stays unnamed, and why the reason moved into the tree

`SemanticElementSchema` and `HtmlElementSchema` are **not** exported and are **not** split into per-tag schemas. Both are FAMILY schemas keyed by a tag `z.enum`: a name bound to either hands a consumer a schema that accepts every tag in the family, not the one node type every other name on that barrel stands for. objectui#8499 recorded exactly that reason when it armed the arms and deferred the naming — exporting the pair "would publish a NAMED authoring surface (`z.enum` families, not per-tag schemas) that this card's ruling does not cover" — and the ruling upheld it. Splitting the families into per-tag schemas was ruled out in the same record, as expansion for a consumer nobody has measured.

⭐ The reason is now recorded where it will survive. A `.changeset/*.md` is consumed and deleted at release, so a reason that lives only in a changeset outlives its own explanation and leaves a deliberate non-export looking exactly like a dropped line. So:

- both families carry `ABSENT_BY_DECISION` rows in `packages/types/src/__tests__/arm-named-export-8784.test.ts`, **quoting** that changeset sentence rather than citing it;
- the non-export is also written on the barrel beside the `layout.zod.js` block, the way `RetiredKanbanNodeSchema`'s already is;
- the two named arms **lose** their ledger rows, because exporting them makes the rows stale and the pin's own stale-row leg fails on a row whose arm is now named.

`ABSENT_PENDING_DECISION` is left in place and empty: it is one of the three answers the pin's failure message offers, so a future card that arms an arm it has no ruling to name still has somewhere to say so.

## ⛔ On this card's framing — corrected by the record, not by editing the filer's text

The card is titled as objectui#7917's defect "recurring one day after its repair" and reads the four omissions as accidental. **That is wrong, and this PR does not carry it.** The omission was declared out loud in objectui#8499's changeset, raised by its ceiling review as a blocking finding, and passed on the surface-widening reason. No one forgot. A decision was deferred, and this change is that decision landing. The filer's text is left as filed; the correction lives in the ruling, in the changeset here, and in the ledger docblock.

Recorded instrument habit that makes the correction reproducible, and which was run on this card before anything was written: before writing "X was omitted", `git grep -n X -- .changeset` — deliberate deferrals in this repo are written there. Run here it returns the 8499 changeset; the control (a symbol written into no changeset) returns nothing, so the finder discriminates rather than matching everything.

## Evidence

Gate results are quoted from each run's own verdict line, exit codes captured before any pipe.

| check | command | result |
|---|---|---|
| affected-package tests | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/` | **185 files / 4251 tests passed**, `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| the pin itself | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/arm-named-export-8784.test.ts` | **1 file / 15 tests passed**, `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| Type Check | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` (all three tsc projects, `tsconfig.test.json` included, so the ledger edit is type-checked) | `VERDICT command-exit 0` |
| Lint | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` | `exit 0` — 0 errors; the 284 warnings are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` in files this PR does not touch |
| Changeset Declaration | `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | `exit 0` — "2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s)" |
| governed surface | `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test PATH PATH PATH` (the three changed paths) | `NOT GOVERNED — 3 path(s) checked against 5 governed surface(s); none matched` |
| package build | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build` (`tsc && vite build && check-dist-completeness`) | `VERDICT command-exit 0` — "dist completeness: 1 package(s) complete (130 emitted files verified)" |
| built-artifact pin | `OBJECTUI_DIST_PINS=1 vitest run --project dist packages/types/` (`zod-subpath-single-module-8598.dist.spec.tsx`, the pin that the shipped `./zod` is ONE module) | **1 file / 5 tests passed**, `VERDICT command-exit 0` |

Dependency-closure build (`pnpm --filter '@object-ui/types^...' build`) is **empty by construction**: `@object-ui/types` is the zero-dependency protocol package, so there is no upstream closure to build.

Remaining required checks — `Test (shard 1/4…4/4)`, `Build & E2E`, `Build Docs` — are repo-wide runs owned by CI.

## The published surface, read as a consumer reads it

Importing the **built** entry (`packages/types/dist/zod/index.zod.js`, the file `exports['./zod']` resolves to) rather than the source, after `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`:

```
--- named on the built ./zod entry (the ruling says these two ARE) ---
  InputShorthandSchema => PRESENT
  UiCalendarSchema => PRESENT
--- absent by decision (the ruling says these are NOT) ---
  SemanticElementSchema => absent
  HtmlElementSchema => absent
  RetiredKanbanNodeSchema => absent
--- behaviour: each new name validates its own node type alone ---
  InputShorthandSchema.safeParse({type:"password"}).success = true
  InputShorthandSchema.safeParse({type:"h1"}).success       = false
  UiCalendarSchema.safeParse({type:"ui:calendar"}).success  = true
  UiCalendarSchema.safeParse({type:"calendar"}).success     = false
--- control: accept set unmoved, union still takes both ---
  AnyComponentSchema.safeParse({type:"ui:calendar"}).success = true
  AnyComponentSchema.safeParse({type:"h1"}).success          = true
  AnyComponentSchema.safeParse({type:"h1ZZ"}).success        = false
```

The last block is the accept-set control: `h1` still validates through the union even though no name is bound to it, and `h1ZZ` is still refused. Nothing widened, nothing narrowed.

## Ablation — three legs, each proved on disk, each restored from `HEAD`

Run **after** the implementation commit, so every restore leg targets `git checkout HEAD -- PATH` with the implementation already in `HEAD`. Each mutation is proved to have reached the disk by counting the anchored text before and after (an editor's exit code proves nothing — a zero-hit `perl -0pi` exits 0), and each restore is proved by comparing `git hash-object` against the `HEAD` blob hash **and** by an empty `git diff HEAD`, never by an exit code. An empty hash is treated as failure, not as "nothing to compare". The script carries `trap restore EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths.

⭐ **No build step is involved, and the ablation is what proves that**: the pin imports `../zod/index.zod.js`, a same-package relative specifier that resolves to `src/zod/index.zod.ts`. Mutating the **source** turns the pin red with nothing rebuilt, which is the measurement — not an assumption about the resolution path.

| leg | mutation (proved on disk) | predicted | observed |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | drop the new `UiCalendarSchema,` barrel line (1 occurrence to 0) | red, naming the arm | **red** — `1 failed \| 14 passed`, `+ "form.zod.ts#UiCalendarSchema [type: ui:calendar]"` |
| 2 | drop the `aside` `ABSENT_BY_DECISION` row (1 to 0) | red, naming the family | **red** — `1 failed \| 13 passed`, `+ "layout.zod.ts#SemanticElementSchema [type: aside, main, header, nav, footer, section, and 1 more]"` |
| 3 | re-add a `ui:calendar` ledger row, i.e. keep the row this PR deletes (0 to 1) | red on the stale-row leg | **red** — `1 failed \| 15 passed (16)`, on "delete the row. A ledger that keeps rows after their reason is gone stops being read" |

Leg 1 shows the new export is load-bearing. Leg 2 shows the `ABSENT_BY_DECISION` rows, not luck, are what keep the two families green. Leg 3 shows that **deleting** the two `email` / `ui:calendar` rows was required rather than cosmetic — leaving them would have been red. Baseline before the legs and the tree after them both verify at the `HEAD` blob hashes, and the final `git status --porcelain` is empty.

## Acceptance notes

Out of scope for this card, **filed as objectui#9406** rather than carried here:

- `packages/types/src/index.ts` (the **TypeScript** root barrel, a different surface from the zod barrel this card rules on) exports neither the `InputShorthandSchema` nor the `UiCalendarSchema` **type** counterpart, though it exports their neighbours `InputSchema` and `CalendarSchema`. Both types are reachable today through the `@object-ui/types/form` subpath, so nothing is blocked; the root spelling is the one that reads TS2305. That is the same shape objectui#7697 filed for `ComboboxOption`, and its repair changeset states it in as many words. The ruling here names one file, `packages/types/src/zod/index.zod.ts`, and touching the TS root barrel would mint two more published names on a surface no one has ruled on — precisely the widening this card exists to refuse doing by reflex. Measured with a probe whose two controls pass in the same compilation pass (`TS2724` on the two root imports; the `/form` subpath import and the `CalendarSchema` root import both clean), and the instrument habit run against `.changeset/` found no record deferring these two from the root barrel. Filed as **objectui#9406**, unassigned and ungraded, asking for the ruling rather than asserting the repair.

Implemented by the ObjectStack `os-dev` agent seat with Claude Code; session `https://claude.ai/code/session_011QreXiyMEqKLN4U5daMPVa`.

⚠️ Attribution is written as prose and as a code span on purpose, and no footer block of my own is sent. This repository has measured that a `PATCH` **unconditionally appends** a second attribution footer even when the submitted body already ends with one, and that it can downgrade a session-URL footer to the bare form — so the footer block is not a durable carrier for a session reference, while a backtick code span in prose is measured to survive. Read back after this edit: the body is byte-identical to what was sent apart from the one footer the platform appends itself.
